Import boundary:
Native list creation, input construction and async-handler preparation precede
native_copy::import_and_store. Before that boundary there is no UR borrower;
exceptions or unsupported/no-group/no-symbol conditions may generic-fallback.
The first action inside the import callback is make_queue. Any exception from
that call, including non-std exceptions and conservatively even argument copies,
is ambiguous and calls shared fail_stop before NativeOwner/Library can unwind.
There is no fallback or retry after import attempt fails.
On return, queue stays local inside helper. Insertion callback takes queue by
reference; lock/allocation/construction failures are caught inside queue's live
scope, before queue destruction. EngineStream copies from a const reference,
not a by-value parameter: a failure allocating a list node does not destroy a
moved temporary inside the callback before the handler. A partial EngineStream
construction can release its shared_ptr member but caller owner is still live;
queue copy failure has no published entry. No application work is submitted
between native creation, import and successful insertion. Failed insertion is
nevertheless fail-stop, avoiding reliance on unverified destructor cleanup.

fail_stop matches existing Runtime fatal: fprintf + fflush(stderr) then _Exit(1).
It does not run stack/static destructors or atexit callbacks. It retains objects
until process termination; OS/driver process teardown is outside this contract.
It does NOT release or repair an orphan UR queue. The LLVM source still has its
raw-handle exception gap. Uncertain partial import cannot continue with a native
handle destroyed by local unwinding. Source retention is the bounded remedy.
Diagnostic stdio itself may block: Main's independent process deadline remains
required, just as for existing fatal. No crash recovery/service continuation.

Normal success remains ownership::keep: queue before list before loader through
EngineStream reverse member destruction. Native Runtime::finish wraps actual
barrier submission, event wait and async check in checked_release. Any exception
(all types) exits before stream/buffers can release. destroy_stream calls finish
before erasure; Runtime destruction drains before destroying its stream list;
Runtime::free drains before USM release. Library dlclose and list destroy results
use the same shared checked_release and cannot continue teardown on failure.
No pending work is released after an unknown drain result. Existing concurrent
stream destruction/use remains outside the API contract.

Preserved gates: defaultOFF, exact frozen STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1; API COPY/notCOMPUTE
nonzero bounded groups; same Runtime context/device; no profiling property on
native queue; serviceEvents uses generic profiling route. COPY-only facade guards
cover compute, memset, parallel_for copy2d, host_task, graph and fork/join.
NonTiming native events use barriers even with forced tag; timing tags refuse.
Existing actualevent/crossqueue dependencies and Prefill host source credits are
unchanged. No host/device atomic or volatile polling. Public raw SYCL access is
not a capability security boundary. v2 includes all v1 production changes.

CPU fixture calls the exact production import_and_store/checked_release/fail_stop
helpers, not a parallel enum. Fake resource destructors emit explicit release
markers. Modes inject after native creation, before import return, after raw
borrower creation, during insertion, failed/throwing drain, list destroy and
loader close. Fatal modes need independent process exit/output checks. The fake
borrower deliberately models the audited raw UR handoff, and does not prove
actual SYCL/UR adapter internals or urQueueRelease counts. There are no hidden
test environment knobs in production. Fixture uses no SYCL/device/library.
GPU fixture is inherited v1 source, manual only/no GPU CTest, tiny actual USM and
crossqueue events/canaries, role refusals/drain. It does not test model/Stager,
actual import exception injection or performance. NVIDIA unavailable/unverified.

No performance, correctness-pass, adapter qualification or adoption claim.

Main owns every build/test/lint/sanitizer/GPU/process/Git/admission operation.
